newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs quickly recover after fall on May output data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs quickly recover after fall on May output data.

text.p: Key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures swiftly rebounded on Friday after initially falling on stronger-than-expected Japanese industrial output data for May.
Industrial output in May rose a preliminary 3.8 percent from the previous month, sparking immediate selling.

But JGBs recovered quickly afterwards because the ministry's forecasts for June and July were weaker than expected, and this fueled a view that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would not raise interest rates before confirming a firm economic recovery in the July-September period, traders said.
The September stood at 123.80 at 0518 GMT after falling sharply to 123.25 soon after the release of the data at 0430 GMT. Thursday's finish was at 123.27.
The ministry forecast a 2.6 percent month-on-month fall for June and a 0.9 percent rise for July.

"The industrial production data was consistent with the BOJ's tankan results, which showed corporate sentiment differed depending on industry," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. "That means no rate rise is unlikely until the BOJ confirms strength in the economic recovery in the critical period between July and September," he said.
